key_insight: The paper shows that small, efficient vision-language models can be trained to make trusted, interpretable anomaly decisions on time-series data—without needing massive multimodal systems. The core breakthrough is building a benchmark that teaches models not just to detect anomalies, but to explain them grounded in the sequence.
problem_solved: Existing time-series anomaly benchmarks usually provide only interval labels, not natural-language explanations. This makes it hard to fine-tune vision-language models for grounded reasoning and reliable, interpretable anomaly detection.
method: Constructs VisAnomBench, a new benchmark for time-series anomaly detection with language-style supervision.
Adapts vision-language reasoning to sequential data so models can localize abnormal regions and produce explanations.
Focuses on efficient, smaller models to improve practicality, trustworthiness, and deployment feasibility.
impact: This matters because practitioners need anomaly detectors that are both accurate and explainable, especially in high-stakes domains like monitoring, healthcare, and industrial systems. The approach lowers the barrier to using multimodal reasoning for time-series tasks by making it more data-efficient and trustworthy.

paper_title: Tiny but Trusted: Efficient Vision-Language Reasoning for Time-Series Anomaly Detection
paper_authors: Xiaona Zhou, Muntasir Wahed, Tianjiao Yu, Constantin Brif, Ismini Lourentzou
